title: Sell Mineral Rights in Smock, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Smock, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Smock in Fayette County? We buy Marcellus interests directly and pay cash, no landman runaround, no lowball guessing.
heroLead: Smock is barely a dot on the map outside Uniontown, but the ground underneath it has the same wet-gas potential that's kept operators busy across the rest of Fayette County for years.
intro: Smock is an unincorporated community just outside Uniontown, built originally around the old coal patch towns that dotted this part of Fayette County. Most families who own minerals near Smock inherited a small tract or a fractional interest tied to a much larger farm that got broken up generations ago, and untangling exactly what's yours can be the hardest part of ever selling it.

The Marcellus wet-gas window reaches this part of Fayette County, and while activity right around Smock isn't as dense as it is further west toward Washington and Greene counties, unit pooling and lease activity have touched a good number of small tracts here.

sections.heading: Small Tracts, Old Deeds, and What They're Worth
paragraphs: A lot of Smock-area interests are small, sometimes a few acres carved out of what was once a much bigger coal patch farm. Small doesn't mean worthless. If your tract sits inside or near an active drilling unit, even a modest fractional interest carries real value, and we buy interests of every size rather than requiring some minimum acreage to bother with.

sections.heading: Deductions and the Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act
paragraphs: Pennsylvania law guarantees a minimum one-eighth royalty on gross value, but it doesn't stop lease-permitted deductions for gathering, compression, and transportation from being applied within that math. If you've noticed your check running smaller than the sale price of gas would suggest, that's almost always the reason, and it's worth reviewing your specific lease language rather than assuming something's wrong.

sections.heading: Selling a Fractional Interest Near Smock
paragraphs: We start with your deed, confirm the fraction you actually own against the recorder of deeds record, check whether your tract sits in an active unit, and give you a clear offer. There's no obligation to accept it, and no pressure to move faster than you're comfortable with.

faqs.question: My tract is only a couple of acres. Is it worth selling?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, especially if it sits within an active unit. Value depends on unit production and your fractional share, not only raw acreage.

faqs.question: How do I confirm my exact fractional interest?
faqs.answer: We review your deed history at the recorder of deeds office alongside any probate or heirship records to confirm the precise share you hold before making an offer.

faqs.question: Does my deed's coal reservation affect the gas rights?
faqs.answer: Not usually. Coal, oil, and gas are commonly severed separately in Fayette County deeds, and we only buy what your specific deed actually grants you in oil and gas.
